clue.text: Take off underclothing, finding impurities

parts.note: to do someone is to take them off, i.e. impersonate them
pants are underwear in British English

explanation.surface: Someone stripping off their underwear and discovering it is not entirely clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' reads as undressing, but it is mimicry: doing an impression of someone. In Britain pants are underpants, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopants are impurities deliberately added to a semiconductor to change its properties.

clue.text: Two months to boil down

explanation.surface: A recipe telling you to let something simmer for an absurdly long two months.
explanation.walkthrough: Any two months will do, so the solver has to find the pair of abbreviations that makes a word: DEC then OCT.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoct is to boil something down to extract its essence.

clue.text: Fix round vessel for cake

indicators.note: the fix goes round the vessel, enclosing it

parts.note: to pin is to fix in place

explanation.surface: Instructions for fastening a round tin or dish to hold a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round vessel' looks like a cake tin, but 'round' belongs to the fix, which goes around the vessel. Parkin is a northern English cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a sticky ginger cake made with oatmeal and treacle, a Yorkshire speciality.

clue.text: Following closely, a lot on site for development

indicators.note: a development site is where things get rebuilt into a new form, as these letters are

explanation.surface: An estate agent's line about a plot of land coming up for building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot on site' reads as a building plot, which hides it as ten letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cars nose to tail are queued so close that each front almost touches the back of the one ahead.

clue.text: Shoot gun if really pressurised, snipers all heading northward

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading from bottom to top
each word's heading is its first letter, and 'all' takes every one

parts.note: the first letters of Gun If Really Pressurised Snipers

explanation.surface: A shootout in which pressured snipers all make a run north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' and 'gun' and 'snipers' all belong to one firefight, but the first word is a plant's shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig of a plant.

clue.text: Humourless dandy recalled getting beaten by racketeer

indicators.note: called back, so the word comes back the other way

parts.note: a player with a racket beats an opponent with an ace, an unreturnable serve

explanation.surface: A dour dandy remembered for being beaten up by a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: A racketeer is usually a gangster; here it is someone holding a tennis racket, and being aced is being beaten by their serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Po-faced means solemn and disapproving, without a trace of humour.

clue.text: Complex in Naples welcoming university in Calabria, say?

definitions.note: Calabria is an example of a peninsula, hence 'say?'

indicators.note: the letters take in the university as a guest
a complex arrangement is an intricate one, so the letters are tangled

explanation.surface: A building complex near Naples that houses a university in Calabria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' reads as a noun, a block of buildings, but it is the anagram instruction. Calabria is the toe of Italy's boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Calabria juts out into the sea with water on three sides, so it is a peninsula.

clue.text: Maverick offering drinks on the house?

definitions.meaning: a maverick is an independent thinker who ignores convention

definitions.note: drinks is plural, while the answer is singular
definitions.meaning: a distilled drink such as whisky or gin

explanation.surface: An unconventional barman who gives away free drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: spirit that is free, as when the landlord pours you a whisky on the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A free spirit is a maverick, someone who goes their own way regardless of convention.

clue.text: Shutting up gutless egotist is immense, as lippy perhaps?

definitions.note: lippy is an example of a cosmetic, hence 'perhaps?'

indicators.note: shutting something up is enclosing it
without its guts only the outside of the word is left

explanation.surface: Silencing a cowardly, puffed-up egotist is a huge relief, and so is shutting up a lippy one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lippy' in the surface means cheeky; as the definition it is British slang for lipstick.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: lippy is British slang for lipstick, one kind of make-up.

clue.text: Stand in river maintaining exercise, upright

indicators.note: to maintain something is to hold it, so the river holds the exercise

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing the word upright reads it from the bottom up

explanation.surface: Someone standing upright in a river as part of an exercise routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand in' looks like it goes with 'river' as in standing in water; it is the definition, to act as a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a deputy acts in someone's place, so to take that role for a while is to stand in.

clue.text: Under discussion, heart unit

indicators.note: being discussed means being spoken about, so the word is heard

parts.note: the heart of an apple, or of a matter, is its core

explanation.surface: A cardiology topic being debated: the heart unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The P and S of corps are silent, so it is said exactly like core.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a military unit, or any organised body of people.

clue.text: Bean soup, nothing less, for seconds?

indicators.note: less means minus, taking the nought out of the soup

explanation.surface: A diner asking whether there is bean soup, and nothing else, for second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' sounds like more food; the question mark flags the other seconds, those who come second.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners-up are those who finish second in a contest.

clue.text: Note: I appreciate that award for a city on the Bay of Bengal

definitions.text: a city on the Bay of Bengal

parts.note: a chit is a short note
ta is British informal for thank you
a gong is British slang for a medal or award

explanation.surface: A thank-you note to someone accepting an award from an Indian or Bangladeshi city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' wants to be a musical letter such as C; it is CHIT. TA and GONG are both British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Chittagong is Bangladesh's main port, on the Bay of Bengal.

clue.text: Material sensed

definitions.meaning: a noun: cloth, here a pressed woollen fabric
a verb in the past tense: perceived by touch or emotion

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two readings: a noun for a fabric and a verb in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is a pressed woollen fabric, and felt is also the past tense of feel.

clue.text: Raise your voice about staff making errors

indicators.note: about means around, so the call goes around the staff

parts.note: sing up! means raise your voice
a crew is a staff of workers

explanation.surface: A manager shouting about staff who keep getting things wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise your voice about' reads as complaining about something, but 'about' puts SING UP around CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: to screw something up is to botch it, so the -ing form matches 'making errors'.

clue.text: Relationships entered into by male artist with desire to eat after smoking a joint

definitions.text: desire to eat after smoking a joint

indicators.note: the relationships are entered, so the male and the artist go inside

parts.note: Edvard Munch, painter of The Scream

explanation.surface: A male artist's love life, tangled up with his appetite after a spliff.
explanation.walkthrough: Any artist could fit; Munch is the one whose name also belongs to the answer's world of eating.
explanation.definitionFit: The munchies is slang for the hunger that comes on after smoking cannabis.

clue.text: Performance killing act

definitions.meaning: the carrying out of a task or a piece of music
the act of putting a condemned person to death

explanation.walkthrough: 'Performance killing act' reads like a critic panning a show; it splits after the first word into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution is the performance of a task, and also the act of putting someone to death.

clue.text: Maybe Celtic sofa initially like a bed?

definitions.note: Celtic is one example of something Scottish, hence 'Maybe'

indicators.note: the sofa contributes only its initial letter

parts.note: a playful coinage: like a cot, which is a bed

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Celtic-style sofa doubles as a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits COTTISH is not a real word. Celtic is also a Glasgow football club, which is one way to be Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtic can describe Scottish culture, or Glasgow's Celtic Football Club.

clue.text: Illicitly, a romance being filmed

indicators.note: done illicitly, the letters are not arranged the proper way

explanation.surface: A secret affair caught on film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Illicitly' belongs so naturally with 'a romance' that it does not read as an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain idiom: a scene in front of a running lens is being recorded, the phrase used in film and television.

clue.text: Kind that's legally able to score in the box

indicators.note: the onside player goes in the box, placed inside it

parts.note: in football a player must be onside for a goal to count

explanation.surface: A generous striker who is onside and free to score in the penalty box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the box' reads as the penalty area, where goals are scored; it is a crate, with ONSIDE placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerate means kind and thoughtful towards others.

clue.text: See 6
Soldiers one threat

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.walkthrough: 'One' can be I, A or ACE; here it is the ace, the one in a deck of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both nouns: a person or thing that endangers others poses a threat, whether a bully or a stray dog.

clue.text: What melts?

indicators.note: melted things lose their shape, and so do these letters

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, a riddle whose answer is a thaw, and it is also an anagram of WHAT with 'melts' as the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue asks for the warm spell that turns ice and snow to water, and the letters of 'What' melt into that very word.

clue.text: Shoe, shocking pink, that is for a dish

parts.note: a pump is a light shoe

indicators.note: shocking suggests a jolt that scrambles the letters

explanation.surface: A fashion note about a shoe in shocking pink.
explanation.walkthrough: Shocking pink is a real vivid colour, so 'shocking' reads as part of the description rather than as the anagram instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpkin pie is a dish, a sweet pie of spiced pumpkin custard.

clue.text: Star in Canis Minor goes round

indicators.note: the little dog goes round the IN, enclosing it

parts.note: Canis Minor is Latin for lesser dog, so a small dog, a pup

explanation.surface: An astronomy note about a star in the constellation Canis Minor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star in Canis Minor' reads as Procyon or another real star; the constellation name is translated literally instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a star or celebrity whose picture is pinned on walls.

clue.text: Dull gospeller to his familiars?

definitions.meaning: without shine or gloss, as a paint finish
Matthew the gospel writer, as his friends would call him

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a gospel writer's friends found him boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The gospeller is Matthew, and those familiar with him would shorten the name to Matt.
explanation.definitionFit: Matt describes a dull finish without shine, as in matt paint.

clue.text: Repeating time after time after time, I love breaking in

indicators.note: the love breaks into the word, splitting it
each piece follows the one before it

parts.note: an era is a period of time
love = zero = O, as in tennis

explanation.surface: A lover saying the same thing over and over, breaking in each time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface phrase 'time after time' hides three separate times, two as the single letter and one as a period; love is zero, as in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with 'Repeating' read as a noun: the doing of something again, as in a loop in computing.

clue.text: Lake where a bore recedes

indicators.note: going back, so the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: A lake where a tidal bore, a wave running upriver, ebbs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' suggests a tidal wave in the surface; it is a dull thing, a drag.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the largest lake in Italy, at the foot of the Alps.

clue.text: Lift near the ground

indicators.note: ground as in milled, so the letters are crushed and remixed

explanation.surface: A lift stopping near the ground floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun, the ground floor, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lift someone, in the sense of raising their spirits, is to encourage them.

clue.text: Tube ending in passage alongside canary, say, in mine

indicators.note: 'in' as a preposition of place puts the pet inside the pit

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
a canary is an example of a pet

indicators.note: only the end of the passage is taken

explanation.surface: A tube running through a mine shaft next to the miners' canary.
explanation.walkthrough: The canary in the mine calls up the old warning bird for gas; here it is simply a pet placed in PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipette is a slender tube for measuring or transferring small amounts of liquid.
